newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian unionist attacked, wounded in Algiers.
newsitem.headline: Algerian unionist attacked, wounded in Algiers.

text.p: Algeria's top trade union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda was seriously wounded in an attack on Tuesday afternoon in central Algiers, Algerian security forces said.

In a statement on the official Algerian news agency APS, the security forces said Benhamouda, leader of the Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA), was attacked in May 1st Square in central Algiers.
"The victim was immediately evacuated to Mustapha hospital where his condition was judged serious," the security forces said.
The security authorities gave no details on how the attack was carried out.

Benhamouda, a former staunch supporter of the government in its battle against Moslem fundamentalists, recently strongly criticised the lack of political activity to resolve the five-year-old conflict.
He said he would set up his own party.
The bustling May 1st Square lies on the edge of the Moslem fundamentalist area of Belcourt where 42 people were killed in a bomb attack last week.
Algeria has been locked in conflict since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election which Islamist fundamentalists were poised to win.
